Name: chrono_policy_extrapolation
Title: Offline RL Should Read the Timestamps: Policy-Space Extrapolation Along the Data-Collection Improvement Direction
Short Hypothesis: Most offline RL datasets are logs of a system that was getting better over time, yet algorithms treat them as an unordered bag of transitions and are therefore fundamentally anchored to the average behavior policy. We hypothesize that the intra-dataset ordering (collection time, or a return-based pseudo-time) defines an improvement direction in policy space, and that extrapolating a short distance along this direction --- in policy parameter/embedding space rather than in a conditioning token --- yields policies that outperform every policy present in the data, with the extrapolation magnitude selectable purely offline using a pessimistic critic.
Related Work: (1) Conservative value-based offline RL (CQL, IQL, TD3+BC, MCQ, RORL, SCQ) explicitly regularizes toward the behavior distribution; its implicit ceiling is the best in-support behavior, and it ignores which part of the log came from a weaker vs. stronger logging policy. (2) Return-conditioned supervised methods (Decision Transformer, RvS, reward-conditioned BC) do use trajectory quality, but extrapolation is attempted at inference by querying an out-of-range return token, which is well documented to fail; we instead extrapolate in weight/feature space and keep the conditioning input in-range. (3) T-REX/D-REX extrapolate a *reward function* from ranked demonstrations and then require online RL; we require no environment interaction and extrapolate the *policy*. (4) Multi-demonstrator / imbalanced-dataset offline RL and filtered %BC use quality labels only to select or reweight data, never to define a direction of improvement. (5) Weight interpolation/extrapolation (model soups, ExPO for LLM alignment, WARP) shows parameter-space extrapolation can amplify alignment in supervised settings; nobody has asked whether an offline RL dataset itself contains an implicit improvement direction that can be amplified this way, nor how to choose the step size without online rollouts. Our contribution is the observation, two concrete instantiations, a fully offline step-size selection rule, and a falsification test (label shuffling) that isolates the ordering signal.
Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning datasets are usually collected by a process that was itself improving: replay buffers of an RL run, successive versions of a deployed recommender, or a sequence of increasingly skilled human operators. Standard offline RL discards this structure, pooling all transitions and then constraining the learned policy to stay near the resulting behavior mixture. We argue this throws away the single most useful signal in the log: the direction in which the data-generating policy was already moving. We introduce Chronological Policy Extrapolation (CPX), which (i) partitions a dataset by collection index (or, when timestamps are unavailable, by a return-based pseudo-time), (ii) fits a progress-conditioned policy whose dependence on the progress variable is linear in parameter or feature space --- either via a hypernetwork/linear-embedding conditioning or via simple weight arithmetic between policies trained on early and late data --- and (iii) extrapolates beyond the last observed progress value, theta = theta_late + alpha (theta_late - theta_early), with alpha chosen entirely offline by maximizing a pessimistic (ensemble-lower-bound) critic score on dataset states. CPX is a wrapper: it applies on top of BC, TD3+BC, IQL, or CQL. On D4RL replay-style and mixed-quality datasets we test three claims: extrapolation exceeds the best policy contained in the data; the gain disappears when progress labels are shuffled, confirming the ordering (not extra capacity) is responsible; and the offline critic ranks alpha well enough to keep regret to an oracle alpha small. We further characterize when extrapolation helps versus catastrophically diverges, giving a practical, essentially free addition to any offline RL pipeline.
Experiments: 1) Datasets with genuine collection order: D4RL hopper/walker2d/halfcheetah medium-replay and full-replay (transitions are stored in buffer order, giving a chronological index); plus two datasets we generate ourselves in an academic budget: (a) save the full SAC replay buffer plus checkpoint IDs for 3 MuJoCo tasks, (b) construct 'staged operator' datasets by rolling out K=5 SAC checkpoints of increasing skill in Adroit/AntMaze-style tasks and labeling stage IDs. 2) Instantiations: (A) Weight arithmetic: train two (or K) copies of the same offline algorithm (BC, TD3+BC, IQL) on the early and late quantiles of the data from a shared initialization and shared minibatch schedule; form theta(alpha)=theta_late + alpha (theta_late - theta_early) for alpha in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}. (B) Progress-conditioned policy: pi(a|s,tau) with tau the normalized collection index injected through a *linear* embedding (or a hypernetwork whose weights are affine in tau), trained on the whole dataset; at test time query tau = 1 + alpha. 3) Offline alpha selection: score each candidate by J_hat(alpha) = E_{s~D}[min_i Q_i(s, pi_alpha(s))] using an IQL/ensemble critic trained once on the full data, optionally with an action-deviation penalty; report Spearman correlation between J_hat(alpha) and true online return, and the normalized-score regret of the selected alpha versus the oracle alpha. 4) Baselines: BC on all data, BC on the last quantile only, top-10% return-filtered BC, TD3+BC, CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer with max and 1.5x-max return-to-go conditioning, and a naive ensemble/soup (alpha=0) to control for averaging effects. 5) Falsification/ablation battery: shuffle the progress labels (gain should vanish); reverse them (should hurt); vary number of buckets K in {2,3,5,10}; corrupt ordering with noise at rates 0-50%; measure monotonicity of per-bucket behavior-policy return and correlate it with the extrapolation gain; replace true timestamps with return-percentile pseudo-time on medium-expert, random-medium mixtures, and antmaze-diverse to test applicability without metadata. 6) Diagnostics: distance of extrapolated actions from dataset actions (to show the method leaves the support in a *directed*, not random, way), critic overestimation on extrapolated actions, and stability across 5 seeds. Metrics: D4RL normalized return, improvement over the best-scoring individual policy/trajectory in the dataset, Spearman rho and regret for alpha selection, and failure rate (fraction of task-seed pairs where the selected alpha underperforms alpha=0).
Risk Factors and Limitations: Replay buffers are only weakly monotonic (SAC performance oscillates), so the estimated improvement direction may be noisy and extrapolation may amplify noise rather than skill. Parameter-space extrapolation is only meaningful if the two endpoint policies are linearly mode-connected; this may require shared initialization and identical training schedules, and may break for large or normalization-heavy networks. The gain may in some tasks reduce to that of simply training on the latest data (we explicitly baseline this). Offline critic-based selection of alpha inherits the well-known unreliability of offline model selection and could pick divergent policies; a conservative default (small alpha) may be needed. Finally, results may be limited to locomotion-style dense-reward benchmarks and may not transfer to sparse-reward, stitching-dependent tasks where no single logging policy is competent.
